sanskrit: te pīḍitā bhṛśaṃ tena raudreṇa sahasā vibho pramūḍhā naiva vividur mṛdhe kṛtyaṃ sma kiṃ cana
english: Sorely pressed by that fierce warrior all at once, O lord, they were so dazed that they could not tell what was to be done in the fray.

sanskrit: nākulis tu śatānīkaḥ saumadattiṃ nararṣabham dvābhyāṃ viddhvānadad dhṛṣṭaḥ śarābhyāṃ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: But Śatānīka, Nakula's son, that scorcher of foes, having pierced Saumadatti, that bull among men, with two arrows, roared aloud in delight.

sanskrit: tathetare raṇe yattās tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ vivyadhuḥ samare tūrṇaṃ saumadattim amarṣaṇam
english: And the others too, steadfast in the battle, swiftly pierced the wrathful Saumadatti, each with three straight-flying shafts.

sanskrit: sa tān prati mahārāja cikṣipe pañca sāyakān ekaikaṃ hṛdi cājaghne ekaikena mahāyaśāḥ
english: Against them, O great king, that warrior of high renown hurled five arrows, striking each one of them in the heart with a single shaft.

sanskrit: tatas te bhrātaraḥ pañca śarair viddhā mahātmanā parivārya rathair vīraṃ vivyadhuḥ sāyakair bhṛśam
english: Then the five brothers, pierced by the shafts of that great-souled one, surrounded the hero with their chariots and pierced him sorely with their arrows.

sanskrit: ārjunis tu hayāṃs tasya caturbhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ preṣayām āsa saṃkruddho yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: But the son of Arjuna, filled with wrath, dispatched his horses to the abode of Yama with four whetted shafts.

sanskrit: bhaimasenir dhanuś chittvā saumadatter mahātmanaḥ nanāda balavan nādaṃ vivyādha ca śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The son of Bhīmasena, having cut the bow of the great-souled Saumadatti, roared a mighty roar and pierced him with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: yaudhiṣṭhiro dhvajaṃ tasya chittvā bhūmāv apātayat nākuliś cāśvayantāraṃ rathanīḍād apāharat
english: The son of Yudhiṣṭhira, cutting down his banner, brought it to the ground, while Nakula's son swept the charioteer from the chariot-box.

sanskrit: sāhadevis tu taṃ jñātvā bhrātṛbhir vimukhīkṛtam kṣurapreṇa śiro rājan nicakarta mahāmanāḥ
english: But the high-minded son of Sahadeva, perceiving him turned aside by his brothers, severed his head, O king, with a razor-headed shaft.

sanskrit: tacchiro nyapatad bhūmau tapanīyavibhūṣitam bhrājayantaṃ raṇoddeśaṃ bālasūryasamaprabham
english: That head, adorned with refined gold, fell to the earth, lighting up that quarter of the battlefield, radiant as the rising sun.

sanskrit: saumadatteḥ śiro dṛṣṭvā nipatat tan mahātmanaḥ vitrastās tāvakā rājan pradudruvur anekadhā
english: Seeing the head of the great-souled Saumadatti falling, your warriors, O king, took fright and fled in many directions.

sanskrit: alambusas tu samare bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam yodhayām āsa saṃkruddho lakṣmaṇaṃ rāvaṇir yathā
english: But Alambusa, full of wrath, fought in battle with the mighty Bhīmasena, as the son of Rāvaṇa fought with Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: saṃprayuddhau raṇe dṛṣṭvā tāv ubhau nararākṣasau vismayaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ praharṣaś cābhavat tadā
english: Seeing those two, the man and the rākṣasa, locked together in combat, wonder and delight then arose in all beings.

sanskrit: ārṣyaśṛṅgiṃ tato bhīmo navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha prahasan rājan rākṣasendram amarṣaṇam
english: Then Bhīma, laughing, O king, pierced the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, that wrathful lord of rākṣasas, with nine whetted shafts.

sanskrit: tad rakṣaḥ samare viddhaṃ kṛtvā nādaṃ bhayāvaham abhyadravat tato bhīmaṃ ye ca tasya padānugāḥ
english: That rākṣasa, pierced in the fight, raised a terrifying roar and rushed upon Bhīma, together with those who followed in his train.

sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ bhīmānugāñ jaghānāśu rathāṃs triṃśad ariṃdamaḥ punaś catuḥśatān hatvā bhīmaṃ vivyādha patriṇā
english: Having pierced Bhīma with five smooth-jointed arrows, that subduer of foes swiftly slew thirty chariots of Bhīma's followers, and again, after slaying four hundred, he pierced Bhīma with a feathered shaft.

sanskrit: so 'tividdhas tadā bhīmo rākṣasena mahābalaḥ niṣasāda rathopasthe mūrchayābhipariplutaḥ
english: Then the mighty Bhīma, deeply pierced by the rākṣasa, sank down upon the floor of his chariot, overwhelmed by a swoon.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ mārutiḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ vikṛṣya kārmukaṃ ghoraṃ bhārasādhanam uttamam alambusaṃ śarais tīkṣṇair ardayām āsa sarvataḥ
english: Regaining his senses, the son of the Wind-god, beside himself with rage, drew his dreadful bow, that supreme weapon of heavy work, and tormented Alambusa on every side with keen arrows.

sanskrit: sa viddho bahubhir bāṇair nīlāñjanacayopamaḥ śuśubhe sarvato rājan pradīpta iva kiṃśukaḥ
english: Pierced by many shafts, that rākṣasa, dark as a heap of black collyrium, shone all over, O king, like a kiṃśuka tree in full blossom.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare bhīmacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ smaran bhrātṛvadhaṃ caiva pāṇḍavena mahātmanā
english: As he was being struck in the fight by the arrows loosed from Bhīma's bow, he remembered the slaying of his brother by the great-souled son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: ghoraṃ rūpam atho kṛtvā bhīmasenam abhāṣata tiṣṭhedānīṃ raṇe pārtha paśya me 'dya parākramam
english: Then, assuming a fearsome form, he addressed Bhīmasena: "Stand now in the battle, O son of Pṛthā, and behold this day my prowess."

sanskrit: bako nāma sudurbuddhe rākṣasapravaro balī parokṣaṃ mama tadvṛttaṃ yad bhrātā me hatas tvayā
english: "There was one named Baka, O fool, a mighty chief among rākṣasas; out of my sight that deed was done, when my brother was slain by you."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato bhīmam antardhānagatas tadā mahātā śaravarṣeṇa bhṛśaṃ taṃ samavākirat
english: Having spoken thus, then, vanishing from sight, he covered Bhīma utterly with a mighty downpour of arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu samare rājann adṛśye rākṣase tadā ākāśaṃ pūrayām āsa śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: But Bhīma in the battle, O king, when the rākṣasa had become invisible, filled the sky with his smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno bhīmena nimeṣād ratham āsthitaḥ jagāma dharaṇīṃ kṣudraḥ khaṃ caiva sahasāgamat
english: Struck by Bhīma, that vile one, in the twinkling of an eye, now mounting his chariot, now reaching the earth, and now suddenly springing into the sky.

sanskrit: uccāvacāni rūpāṇi cakāra subahūni ca uccāvacās tathā vāco vyājahāra samantataḥ
english: He took on many forms, high and low, and uttered on every side voices loud and faint.

sanskrit: tena pāṇḍavasainyānāṃ mṛditā yudhi vāraṇāḥ hayāś ca bahavo rājan pattayaś ca tathā punaḥ rathebhyo rathinaḥ petus tasya nunnāḥ sma sāyakaiḥ
english: By him the elephants of the Pāṇḍava army were crushed in the fight, and many horses too, O king, and foot-soldiers as well; and the chariot-warriors, struck by his arrows, fell from their chariots.

sanskrit: śoṇitodāṃ rathāvartāṃ hastigrāhasamākulām chatrahaṃsāṃ kardaminīṃ bāhupannagasaṃkulām
english: With blood for its water, chariots for its whirlpools, thronged with elephants for its crocodiles, parasols for its swans, mire for its silt, and crowded with severed arms for its snakes—

sanskrit: nadīṃ pravartayām āsa rakṣogaṇasamākulām vahantīṃ bahudhā rājaṃś cedipāñcālasṛñjayān
english: —he set flowing a river teeming with hosts of rākṣasas, bearing along in many places, O king, the Cedis, the Pāñcālas, and the Sṛñjayas.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā samare rājan vicarantam abhītavat pāṇḍavā bhṛśasaṃvignāḥ prāpaśyaṃs tatsya vikramam
english: As he ranged thus fearlessly through the battle, O king, the Pāṇḍavas, deeply troubled, beheld his prowess.

sanskrit: tāvakānāṃ tu sainyānāṃ praharṣaḥ samajāyata vāditraninadaś cograḥ sumahāṃl lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: But among your troops great delight arose, and there rose a fierce and mighty din of instruments that made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ tava sainyasya pāṇḍavaḥ nāmṛṣyata yathā nāgas talaśabdaṃ samīritam
english: Hearing that dreadful clamor of your host, the son of Pāṇḍu could not brook it, even as an elephant cannot brook the clapping of hands.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhābhitāmrākṣo nirdahann iva pāvakaḥ saṃdadhe tvāṣṭram astraṃ sa svayaṃ tvaṣṭeva māriṣa
english: Then, his eyes red with wrath and scorching like a blazing fire, he fitted the weapon of Tvaṣṭṛ, himself like Tvaṣṭṛ in person, O sire.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrāṇi prādurāsan samantataḥ taiḥ śarais tava sainyasya vidrāvaḥ sumahān abhūt
english: Then thousands of arrows appeared on every side, and by those arrows a great rout of your army was wrought.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ preṣitaṃ tena bhīmasenena saṃyuge rākṣasasya mahāmāyāṃ hatvā rākṣasam ārdayat
english: That weapon, loosed by Bhīmasena in the encounter, after destroying the great magic of the rākṣasa, tormented the rākṣasa himself.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno bahudhā bhīmasenena rākṣasaḥ saṃtyajya saṃyuge bhīmaṃ droṇānīkam upādravat
english: That rākṣasa, struck in many ways by Bhīmasena, abandoning Bhīma in the encounter, ran toward the division of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nirjite rājan rākṣasendre mahātmanā anādayan siṃhanādaiḥ pāṇḍavāḥ sarvatodiśam
english: When that lord of rākṣasas had been vanquished by the great-souled one, O king, the Pāṇḍavas made all the quarters resound with their lion-roars.

sanskrit: apūjayan mārutiṃ ca saṃhṛṣṭās te mahābalam prahrādaṃ samare jitvā yathā śakraṃ marudgaṇāḥ
english: And, filled with joy, they honored the mighty son of the Wind-god, as the hosts of the Maruts honored Śakra when he had vanquished Prahlāda in battle.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca alambusaṃ tathā yuddhe vicarantam abhītavat haiḍimbaḥ prayayau tūrṇaṃ vivyādha ca śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: As Alambusa ranged thus fearlessly through the battle, the son of Hiḍimbā advanced swiftly upon him and pierced him with sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: tayoḥ pratibhayaṃ yuddham āsīd rākṣasasiṃhayoḥ kurvator vividhā māyāḥ śakraśambarayor iva
english: Terrible was the combat of those two lions among rākṣasas, as they wrought their manifold illusions, like that of Śakra and Śambara.

sanskrit: alambuso bhṛśaṃ kruddho ghaṭotkacam atāḍayat ghaṭotkacas tu viṃśatyā nārācānāṃ stanāntare alambusam atho viddhvā siṃhavad vyanadan muhuḥ
english: Alambusa, exceedingly wrathful, struck Ghaṭotkaca; but Ghaṭotkaca, having pierced Alambusa between the breasts with twenty iron shafts, roared again and again like a lion.

sanskrit: tathaivālambuso rājan haiḍimbaṃ yuddhadurmadam viddhvā viddhvānadad dhṛṣṭaḥ pūrayan khaṃ samantataḥ
english: In the same way Alambusa, O king, piercing again and again the son of Hiḍimbā, that warrior maddened with battle, roared in delight, filling the sky on every side.

sanskrit: tathā tau bhṛśasaṃkruddhau rākṣasendrau mahābalau nirviśeṣam ayudhyetāṃ māyābhir itaretaram
english: Thus those two mighty lords of rākṣasas, exceedingly enraged, fought each other without distinction by means of their illusions.

sanskrit: māyāśatasṛjau dṛptau mohayantau parasparam māyāyuddhe sukuśalau māyāyuddham ayudhyatām
english: Sending forth a hundred illusions, proud, bewildering each other, well skilled in the warfare of illusion, they fought a battle of illusion.

sanskrit: yāṃ yāṃ ghaṭotkaco yuddhe māyāṃ darśayate nṛpa tāṃ tām alambuso rājan māyayaiva nijaghnivān
english: Whatever illusion Ghaṭotkaca displayed in the fight, O king, that very illusion Alambusa, O monarch, destroyed by illusion in turn.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā yudhyamānaṃ tu māyāyuddhaviśāradam alambusaṃ rākṣasendraṃ dṛṣṭvākrudhyanta pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Seeing Alambusa, that lord of rākṣasas, fighting thus and skilled in the warfare of illusion, the Pāṇḍavas grew wroth.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ bhṛśasaṃkruddhāḥ sarvataḥ pravarā rathaiḥ abhyadravanta saṃkruddhā bhīmasenādayo nṛpa
english: Greatly enraged, those foremost warriors, Bhīmasena and the rest, O king, rushed upon him in their wrath from every side with their chariots.

sanskrit: ta enaṃ koṣṭhakīkṛtya rathavaṃśena māriṣa sarvato vyakiran bāṇair ulkābhir iva kuñjaram
english: Hemming him in with the array of their chariots, O sire, they showered him from all sides with arrows, as men beset an elephant with firebrands.

sanskrit: sa teṣām astravegaṃ taṃ pratihatyāstramāyayā tasmād rathavrajān mukto vanadāhād iva dvipaḥ
english: Having warded off the force of their weapons by the magic of his own weapons, he broke free from that ring of chariots like an elephant escaping a forest fire.

sanskrit: sa visphārya dhanur ghoram indrāśanisamasvanam mārutiṃ pañcaviṃśatyā bhaimaseniṃ ca pañcabhiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tribhir viddhvā sahadevaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: Twanging his dreadful bow, whose sound was like the thunderbolt of Indra, he pierced the son of the Wind-god with twenty-five shafts, the son of Bhīmasena with five, Yudhiṣṭhira with three, and Sahadeva with seven.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ ca trisaptatyā drupadeyāṃś ca māriṣa pañcabhiḥ pañcabhir viddhvā ghoraṃ nādaṃ nanāda ha
english: And having pierced Nakula with seventy-three shafts and the sons of Drupada each with five, O sire, he uttered a dreadful roar.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaseno navabhiḥ sahadevaś ca pañcabhiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śatenaiva rākṣasaṃ pratyavidhyata nakulaś ca catuḥṣaṣṭyā draupadeyās tribhis tribhiḥ
english: Bhīmasena pierced that rākṣasa in return with nine shafts, Sahadeva with five, Yudhiṣṭhira with a hundred, Nakula with sixty-four, and the sons of Draupadī each with three.

sanskrit: haiḍimbo rākṣasaṃ viddhvā yuddhe pañcāśatā śaraiḥ punar vivyādha saptatyā nanāda ca mahābalaḥ
english: The son of Hiḍimbā, having pierced that rākṣasa in the fight with fifty arrows, pierced him again with seventy, and the mighty one roared aloud.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāsaḥ sarvatas tair mahārathaiḥ prativivyādha tān sarvān pañcabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: That mighty bowman, deeply pierced on all sides by those great chariot-warriors, pierced them all in return, each with five shafts.

sanskrit: taṃ kruddhaṃ rākṣasaṃ yuddhe pratikruddhas tu rākṣasaḥ haiḍimbo bharataśreṣṭha śarair vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: That rākṣasa, the son of Hiḍimbā, O best of the Bharatas, enraged in turn against the enraged rākṣasa in the fight, pierced him with seven arrows.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā rākṣasendro mahābalaḥ vyasṛjat sāyakāṃs tūrṇaṃ svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān
english: That mighty lord of rākṣasas, deeply pierced by the strong one, swiftly loosed arrows feathered with gold and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: te śarā nataparvāṇo viviśū rākṣasaṃ tadā ruṣitāḥ pannagā yadvad girim ugrā mahābalāḥ
english: Those smooth-jointed arrows then entered the rākṣasa as fierce and mighty serpents in their fury enter a mountain.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavā rājan samantān niśitāñ śarān preṣayām āsur udvignā haiḍimbaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, O king, troubled, dispatched sharpened arrows from all sides, and so did Ghaṭotkaca, the son of Hiḍimbā.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare pāṇḍavair jitakāśibhiḥ dagdhādrikūṭaśṛṅgābhaṃ bhinnāñjanacayopamam
english: As he was being struck in the battle by the Pāṇḍavas flushed with victory, he seized that rākṣasa—like the scorched peak of a mountain, like a riven heap of black collyrium—

sanskrit: samutkṣipya ca bāhubhyām āvidhya ca punaḥ punaḥ niṣpipeṣa kṣitau kṣipraṃ pūrṇakumbham ivāśmani
english: —and lifting him up with both arms and whirling him round again and again, he swiftly dashed him upon the earth, as one dashes a full pitcher against a rock.

sanskrit: balalāghavasaṃpannaḥ saṃpanno vikrameṇa ca bhaimasenī raṇe kruddhaḥ sarvasainyāny abhīṣayat
english: Endowed with strength and dexterity, and endowed with prowess as well, the son of Bhīmasena, wrathful in the fight, struck terror into all the troops.

sanskrit: sa visphuṭitasarvāṅgaś cūrṇitāsthivibhūṣaṇaḥ ghaṭotkacena vīreṇa hataḥ sālakaṭaṅkaṭaḥ
english: With all his limbs shattered and the ornaments of his bones ground to powder, that rākṣasa Sālakaṭaṅkaṭa was slain by the hero Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: tataḥ sumanasaḥ pārthā hate tasmin niśācare cukruśuḥ siṃhanādāṃś ca vāsāṃsy ādudhuvuś ca ha
english: Then the sons of Pṛthā, joyful at heart when that night-ranger was slain, raised lion-roars and waved their garments.

sanskrit: tāvakāś ca hataṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasendraṃ mahābalam alambusaṃ bhīmarūpaṃ viśīrṇam iva parvatam hāhākāram akurvanta sainyāni bharatarṣabha
english: And your troops, O bull of the Bharatas, seeing that mighty lord of rākṣasas, Alambusa of fearsome form, slain like a mountain crumbled to ruin, raised a cry of woe.

sanskrit: janāś ca tad dadṛśire rakṣaḥ kautūhalānvitāḥ yadṛcchayā nipatitaṃ bhūmāv aṅgārakaṃ yathā
english: And the people beheld that rākṣasa, filled with wonder, fallen by chance to the earth like the planet Mars.

sanskrit: ghaṭotkacas tu tad dhatvā rakṣo balavatāṃ varam mumoca balavan nādaṃ balaṃ hatveva vāsavaḥ
english: And Ghaṭotkaca, having slain that rākṣasa, foremost among the mighty, let forth a powerful roar, as Vāsava did when he had slain Bala.

sanskrit: sa pūjyamānaḥ pitṛbhiḥ sabāndhavair; ghaṭotkacaḥ karmaṇi duṣkare kṛte ripuṃ nihatyābhinananda vai tadā; alambusaṃ pakvam alambusaṃ yathā
english: Honored by his fathers and kinsmen for that hard deed accomplished, Ghaṭotkaca then, having slain his foe, rejoiced indeed, having taken Alambusa as one gathers a ripe āḍambusa fruit.

sanskrit: tato ninādaḥ sumahān samutthitaḥ; saśaṅkhanānāvidhabāṇaghoṣavān niśamya taṃ pratyanadaṃs tu kauravās; tato dhvanir bhuvanam athāspṛśad bhṛśam
english: Then a great clamor arose, mingled with conch-blasts and the din of arrows of every kind; and hearing it the Kauravas roared in answer, and that sound thereupon touched the very world with its might.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhāradvājaṃ kathaṃ yuddhe yuyudhāno 'bhyavārayat saṃjayācakṣva tattvena paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How did Yuyudhāna withstand the son of Bharadvāja in the battle? Tell me truly, Saṃjaya, for great is my curiosity.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan mahāprājña saṃgrāmaṃ lomaharṣaṇam droṇasya pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ yuyudhānapurogamaiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king of great wisdom, of the hair-raising battle of Droṇa with the Pāṇḍavas, led on by Yuyudhāna.

sanskrit: vadhyamānaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā yuyudhānena māriṣa abhyadravat svayaṃ droṇaḥ sātyakiṃ satyavikramam
english: Seeing his force being struck down by Yuyudhāna, O sire, Droṇa himself rushed upon Sātyaki of unfailing prowess.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā bhāradvājaṃ mahāratham sātyakiḥ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samārpayat
english: As that great chariot-warrior, the son of Bharadvāja, came swiftly on, Sātyaki met him with twenty-five small arrows.

sanskrit: droṇo 'pi yudhi vikrānto yuyudhānaṃ samāhitaḥ avidhyat pañcabhis tūrṇaṃ hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Droṇa too, valiant in the fight and intent, swiftly pierced Yuyudhāna with five gold-feathered arrows whetted on stone.

sanskrit: te varma bhittvā sudṛḍhaṃ dviṣatpiśitabhojanāḥ abhyagur dharaṇīṃ rājañ śvasanta iva pannagāḥ
english: Those shafts, feeders on the flesh of foes, having pierced his stout armor, entered the earth, O king, hissing like serpents.

sanskrit: dīrghabāhur abhikruddhas tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ droṇaṃ pañcāśatāvidhyan nārācair agnisaṃnibhaiḥ
english: The long-armed warrior, enraged like an elephant goaded by the hook, pierced Droṇa with fifty iron shafts resembling fire.

sanskrit: bhāradvājo raṇe viddho yuyudhānena satvaram sātyakiṃ bahubhir bāṇair yatamānam avidhyata
english: The son of Bharadvāja, swiftly pierced in the battle by Yuyudhāna, pierced in return the striving Sātyaki with many arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho maheṣvāso bhūya eva mahābalaḥ sātvataṃ pīḍayām āsa śatena nataparvaṇā
english: Then that mighty bowman of great strength, enraged once more, oppressed the Sātvata with a hundred smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare bhāradvājena sātyakiḥ nābhyapadyata kartavyaṃ kiṃ cid eva viśāṃ pate
english: Sātyaki, being struck down in the battle by the son of Bharadvāja, could find nothing whatever that should be done, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇavadanaś cāpi yuyudhāno 'bhavan nṛpa bhāradvājaṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā visṛjantaṃ śitāñ śarān
english: And Yuyudhāna, O king, grew downcast of countenance, seeing the son of Bharadvāja in the battle loosing his sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: taṃ tu saṃprekṣya te putrāḥ sainikāś ca viśāṃ pate prahṛṣṭamanaso bhūtvā siṃhavad vyanadan muhuḥ
english: Beholding him thus, O lord of peoples, your sons and your soldiers, their hearts filled with joy, roared again and again like lions.
